summary:
MARS EXPLORER 360 is a digital Martian exploration mapping concept designed to help future astronauts plan safer and more effective surface missions on Mars. The project focuses on the Jezero Crater region and combines multiple types of planetary science information into a unified exploration interface.

The concept brings together terrain and elevation information, rover observations, environmental conditions, and mission safety considerations. It aims to help explorers identify potential hazards, understand the surrounding landscape, select suitable routes, and locate scientifically interesting destinations.

By presenting complex planetary information in an accessible visual format, MARS EXPLORER 360 demonstrates how NASA mission data can support future human exploration of Mars. The project is designed as an educational prototype that can be expanded with additional live data and interactive mapping capabilities.
details: MARS EXPLORER 360 is a browser-based educational prototype designed to demonstrate how multiple Mars mission datasets can support future human surface exploration. The prototype focuses on Jezero Crater, the landing and exploration region of NASA's Perseverance rover. It presents a schematic exploration map with selectable route, hazard and science-location layers. The project brings together several important data categories: 1. Optical and orbital mapping: Mars Trek provides access to orbital imagery and high-resolution Jezero map layers. 2. Terrain information: Elevation and surface context can help identify potential obstacles and suitable exploration areas. 3. Weather information: NASA's MEDA instrument on Perseverance measures wind, temperature, humidity and atmospheric dust. 4. Radiation information: NASA's RAD instrument on Curiosity measures the radiation environment at Gale Crater. This is used as scientific reference context, not as a live Jezero measurement. The interface is designed to make scientific information easier to understand and organize for mission planning. It highlights the importance of checking terrain, environmental conditions and scientific targets before a Marswalk. Technology: HTML, CSS and JavaScript were used to create the browser prototype. Python was used to generate the project presentation. Creative contribution: The project combines multiple mission information categories into one simple visual planning concept that can be expanded with real map services and verified scientific datasets. Limitations: Route lines and hazard markers are illustrative and are not certified navigation data. Future development will integrate live map services, measured terrain information and validated environmental observations. Super Intelligence disclosure: ChatGPT assisted with project writing, code generation, design structure and presentation preparation. AI-assisted elements are disclosed in the prototype and presentation.
